proposals.title: Integrated Multi-Scale Quality Control and Correction in Spatial Transcriptomics
proposals.summary: This analysis integrates spatial geometry with gene expression profiling to detect and correct contamination in spatial transcriptomics data. It employs multi-scale assessment, including iterative dimensionality reduction and neighborhood graph construction to identify outlier spots likely resulting from spot-to-cell misassignments. Using differential expression analysis of established marker genes, the method refines its detection of contaminated regions. Corrections are then applied through spatially guided, model-based normalization that preserves true anatomical boundaries. Validation against gold-standard tissue annotations ensures improved marker specificity and accurate spatial domain delineation.

proposals.title: Iterative Dimensionality Reduction and Neighborhood Graph Optimization for Contamination Detection
proposals.summary: This proposal leverages iterative dimensionality reduction coupled with optimized spatial neighborhood graph construction to unmask subtle contamination artifacts in spatial transcriptomics data. By evaluating clusters for stability and identifying outlier spots through integrated geometry and expression profiles, the method uses sensitivity analyses to fine-tune detection parameters. Differential expression comparisons with known marker signals validate the identified artifacts, ensuring that subsequent corrections retain the biological signal while addressing misassignments effectively.

proposals.title: Differential Expression-Guided Contamination Correction in Spatial Transcriptomics
proposals.summary: Focused on the power of differential gene expression, this approach systematically compares spot-level expression profiles against established marker genes to flag regions with mixed signatures. Spots suspected of contamination from nearby cells are identified and corrected using a targeted, local model-based normalization strategy. This methodology ensures that true expression gradients are maintained while spurious signals are removed, leading to enhanced marker specificity and improved cell-type assignment accuracy. Validation against gold-standard annotations further underscores the robustness of the corrections.

proposals.title: Local Model-Based Normalization for Spot-to-Cell Correction in Spatial Data
proposals.summary: This proposal describes a localized correction framework specifically designed to repair contamination in spatial transcriptomics. After identifying anomalous spots through combined spatial and gene expression assessments, the method applies a local model-based normalization to adjust signal intensities within defined neighborhoods. This ensures that corrections respect fine anatomical boundaries and avoid over-smoothing genuine expression patterns. Differential expression tests are integrated to verify that adjustments successfully mitigate contamination while sustaining true biological variation.

proposals.title: Sensitivity and Stability Analysis in Spatial Transcriptomic Correction Workflows
proposals.summary: To ensure robust contamination detection, this workflow incorporates thorough sensitivity and stability analyses within the spatial transcriptomics pipeline. By iteratively testing parameters in dimensionality reduction, threshold selection, and neighborhood graph construction, the method identifies the most stable clusters and optimizes its ability to flag contaminated spots. Integrated differential expression testing against known markers and validation with gold-standard annotations further substantiate the reliability of the corrections, enhancing overall quality control.

proposals.title: Adaptive Thresholding for Outlier Detection in Spatial Transcriptomics
proposals.summary: This analysis emphasizes the development of adaptive thresholding techniques to pinpoint outlier capture regions exhibiting potential spot-to-cell misassignments. By dynamically setting thresholds informed by both spatial geometry and gene expression data, the method identifies spots with aberrant expression signatures relative to their local tissue context. Subsequent differential expression analysis validates the contamination signal, ensuring that only spurious signals are corrected while genuine anatomical boundaries and cell-type distinctions remain intact.

proposals.title: Gold-Standard Benchmarking for Spatial Domain Delineation and Marker Specificity
proposals.summary: Recognizing the importance of reliable validation, this strategy integrates gold-standard tissue annotations to benchmark the quality of contamination correction in spatial transcriptomics. After initial detection using combined spatial geometry and gene expression analytics, candidate corrections undergo rigorous differential expression validation against established marker genes. This systematic comparison with annotated tissue regions ensures that corrections enhance marker specificity and accurately delineate spatial domains, thereby improving the reliability of downstream biological interpretations.

proposals.title: Comprehensive Integrated Multi-Scale Correction Approach for Spatial Quality Control
proposals.summary: This end-to-end proposal presents a comprehensive pipeline that unites multi-scale spatial analyses, adaptive thresholding, iterative dimensionality reduction, and local normalization methods to address contamination in spatial transcriptomics. By simultaneously leveraging spatial context and gene expression profiles, the methodology accurately identifies and corrects misassigned spots. Sensitivity analyses and differential expression validation underscore the robustness of the approach, ensuring that true anatomical boundaries are maintained and that downstream cell-type assignments and spatial domain delineations are reliable.

plan.user_request: Coordinate TissueAgent domain agents to propose exactly 8 computational spatial-omics analyses most likely performed in the hidden paper, using a three-step draft → critique → synthesis workflow that writes JSON artifacts to the specified hypothesis paths.

steps.title: Draft spatial-omics proposal candidates
steps.description: Have the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) read the provided public background and generate a diverse set of candidate computational spatial-omics analysis proposals related to spatial quality control and contamination/misassignment of spots. Each candidate should include at least a tentative title and descriptive text, and all candidates must be written to `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` as a concrete JSON file on disk; no analyses are executed at this stage.
steps.reasoning: A specialized spatial cross-validation–oriented planner is best suited to propose rich, geometry- and expression-aware candidate analyses aligned with the spot-contamination problem. Producing an explicit draft JSON artifact provides a tangible, reviewable set of ideas for downstream critique and refinement while keeping this step purely proposal-generating rather than executing any analysis.
steps.assignment_rationale: The spatial_cv_agent is explicitly required for the TA+CV treatment to generate the initial set of spatially informed draft analysis proposals and is designed to write the audited draft proposals JSON artifact.

steps.title: Critique draft analysis proposals
steps.description: Use the Critic Agent to read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and produce a structured critical assessment for each candidate analysis, including comments on plausibility, faithfulness to the given background, potential redundancy, feasibility, and expected informativeness for spatial QC. The Critic Agent must save its review as a concrete JSON file at `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` without altering the draft proposals or running any analyses.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated critic pass helps filter and improve the draft proposals by identifying weak, redundant, or misaligned ideas before final selection. Writing a standalone `critique.json` artifact makes the evaluation transparent and provides explicit guidance for the synthesis step, while maintaining a strict separation between proposal generation and execution.
steps.assignment_rationale: The critic_agent is purpose-built for reviewing candidate spatial paper analyses and producing a structured critique, matching the requirement to write only the critique.json artifact without modifying proposals.

steps.title: Synthesize final eight proposals
steps.description: Have the Hypothesis/Synthesis Agent read both `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` and then select, refine, and, if needed, merge or discard candidates to produce exactly 8 final computational spatial-omics analysis proposals that best match the hidden paper’s likely analyses given the background. The agent must write a concrete JSON file to `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json` whose only top-level key is `proposals`, mapped to an array of exactly 8 items, where each item contains only `title` and a detailed `summary` describing the proposed analysis; this step does not execute any analysis, only specifies them.
steps.reasoning: This synthesis step turns the critiqued draft set into the required final deliverable by enforcing the format and cardinality constraints (exactly 8 proposals with `title` and detailed `summary` only) while using the critique to maximize plausibility, diversity, and alignment with the spatial QC problem. Writing `final_proposals.json` in the specified structure ensures downstream consumers can reliably treat it as the single authoritative proposal set.
steps.assignment_rationale: The hypothesis_agent is the synthesis-focused agent that turns drafts plus critique into a final set of exactly eight spatial analysis proposals, writing the required final_proposals.json in the specified format.

provenance.justification: The plan adapts the draft → critic → finalize structure from the `paper_hypothesis_generation` template but collapses it into exactly three steps, omits any PDF or dataset ingestion, and focuses solely on proposal synthesis rather than hypothesis testing. Step (1) is explicitly assigned to the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) as required by the TA+CV treatment, while steps (2) and (3) are aligned with the Critic and Hypothesis/Synthesis agents’ advertised critique and final-synthesis outputs. No template is used as a candidate analysis; templates inform only the workflow pattern.
